notes.title: LA Noire's cyberpunk sibling is going cheap, and it's an absolute must-play
notes.content:
I've said it before and I'll say it again: LA Noire is the best videogame ever made. Its magnificent storytelling, faithful historical setting, and treatment of veteran life in post-WWII America puts it head and shoulders above any RPG I've ever played - and the soundtrack certainly helps, too. But, last year, Critical Hit Games' Nobody Wants to Die came along, almost giving LA Noire a run for its money with its snazzy art-deco cyberpunk setting and brain-teasing mysteries. While it still doesn't touch Rockstar's epic, it's an absolute must play.

notes.title: Dev Log: Thank You
notes.content:
[h2]Thank you.[/h2]
After launching Nobody Wants to Die two weeks ago, we are beyond grateful to see so many of you taking on the case. Seeing the city of New York 2329 through your own eyes and giving everyone the full experience of complete and utter immersion was truly important to us.   

So, we handed the dossier to you to be the first to uncover clues and the stories they hold. We made this game for you and are thrilled our community were able to be some of the first to play and dive into the moral dilemmas of eternal life with no bias or preconceptions. 

The response from you – the players – has been incredible, especially with this being our very first game as Critical Hit Games. We are reading your comments, seeing your reactions, and watching you make the story into your own – and loving every second of it. While creating our vision of a dystopian New York City was enormously exciting, watching you all experience it has been truly remarkable.  


[h2]More than half a million trailer views [/h2]

notes.title: Nobody Wants to Die review - a dazzling tech-noir debut
notes.content:
There he was, Edward Green - an immortal god brought down under the weight of his own gravity and a length of rope from the local supply store. The once-blossoming tree in his atrium - his own personal Eden - a charred husk barely hanging in there like a prize fighter down to his last legs. It doesn't take a genius to figure out that Green was murdered, and in Nobody Wants to Die there's only one man with a worldview cynical enough to see through the layers of high society bullshit obfuscating the truth - detective James Karra.

notes.title: Cyberpunk adventure Nobody Wants to Die feels like if you made an entire game out of the boring no-combat intro of a triple-A FPS
notes.content: Nobody Wants to Die begins with two 2010s storytelling flourishes that made me groan. First, we've got some dead wife hallucinations up in here, the favored psychiatric symptom of tough guy protagonists everywhere. The second was the main character, whose name I already forget, making a noise like "Hnnnnrrrraaaaagggh" and looking down at his hands clenching and unclenching while the screen kind of pulses and goes all blurry. This guy has a terminal case of Xbox 360 FPS protagonitis... Read more.

Under the rain-soaked neon lights of far-future New York, it's up to hard-boiled detectives like James Karra to pick up the police's slack and keep the peace. If you're getting heavy L.A. Noire vibes from this so far, you're not wrong. [h2]Music[/h2]
As a narrative-driven game, music plays a very important role in setting the scene and fulfilling the immersive experience that we wanted to produce with Nobody Wants to Die. 

Music is essential in helping us shape the emotions players feel throughout the course of the game – setting the rhythm and atmosphere for New York, 2329. 

With the music being such a crucial aspect of the game, we knew we could only trust award-winning composer, Mikolai Stroinski, with such a task. His previous work on titles including; [i]The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt, League of Legends, Age of Empires[/i], made him the natural choice in creating the sound of a dystopian New York noir story. 

Imbued with a sense of dark intrigue, the soundtrack’s melodic and moody theme encapsulates the noir essence of the game, putting players into the shoes of Detective James Karra.

notes.title: Dev Log | World Building
notes.content:
Hello everyone,

After revealing a look at the gameplay for Nobody Wants to Die, we have been overwhelmed with the response and support we have received. As a small team from Wrocław, Poland, we could never have expected such a huge response.  

With one month until you enter this world, we invite you to take a look into the creation process and explore the world of Nobody Wants to Die – beginning with some early concept art and insight into the story we have weaved. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44922101/0d52c0ac7b57e912fb233c5fee025febfb5b0897.jpg[/img]

Nobody Wants to Die is an interactive noir story set in a dystopian New York City, where you’ll play as Detective James Karra investigating crime scenes to uncover the mysteries of the city’s elite. 

We wanted to create a thought-provoking narrative for players by only making only one metaphysical change to the current world we live in – the possibility of consciousness transfer. This change alone changes everything. It pulls into question our current values, way of thinking, way of living, and the rules of Western civilization – in such a way that perfectly creates a dark vision of the future. 

We hope to inspire players to think about contemporary values, the rules of the world, and what is important in life – there are even some in-game choices and conflicts connected to that for players to tackle with. 

[h2]New York, 2329[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44922101/767bdb1a7637eb11499eca6699c21e8b79e52766.jpg[/img]
[i]Admiring from above, you let your legs dangle off the ledge of a towering skyscraper. You watch the neon signs and billboards flicker and illuminate an otherwise dark city.[/i]

New York is one of the hearts of contemporary utilisation. We wanted Nobody Wants to Die to say something about the contemporary culture of the Western world, making New York City the prime location for the narrative to unfold. Our futuristic vision was a huge metropolis that would spread and grow in every direction. 

[h2]James Karra’s Apartment[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44922101/5f1f4196177a83a686628f49e0f2e2f8daaee5de.jpg[/img]
[i]You arrive back at your apartment – it's not much, but it’s a place to think. You realise you left a window cracked as you hear the faint whir of traffic outside. The city that never sleeps, makes damn sure that you won’t either as the apartment glows under the city’s harsh neon signs. [/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44922101/ba2296e6efb8d41343756d77986ea8a9422791e7.jpg[/img]
Throughout the game you will retreat into the confines of James’ apartment, where you will piece together the evidence and analyse clues to draw out the truth. 

James, a 120-year-old jaded cop, and Sara, fresh to the force in her late 20s, are our two protagonists in this narrative. They contrast each other with different motivations and goals becoming apparent throughout the narrative. By playing as James, you’ll get to know your investigation partner Sara to be an especially multifaceted character with secrets and motivations of her own that you’ll unravel as you move through your investigation. 


We are excited to share more about the game as we approach July 17 and look forward to welcoming you to New York, 2329 soon. 

- Critical Hit Games

notes.title: New detective game is LA Noire, but with a cyberpunk twist
notes.content:
LA Noire is one of those games that's always just been there for me. It was my favorite as a teenager, then I wrote my Master's thesis on it - wherever I have gone in life, Cole, Jack, Elsa, and the crew have followed. While some cross their fingers tight and hope for a sequel, I've always argued that we don't need an LA Noire 2; in fact a follow-up would just ruin the first game entirely. But I'm all for a spiritual sequel, and Nobody Wants to Die from Critical Hit Games may just be the thing I've been looking for.

notes.title: Welcome to Nobody Wants to Die
notes.content:
We are Critical Hit Games, an independent studio of seasoned game developers based in Wrocław, Poland. Last week, our inaugural project, [i][b]Nobody Wants to Die[/b][/i], was revealed to the world in partnership with IGN to an overwhelming result.

We’re excited to share that we have reached more than [b]1.4 million views[/b] on our announce trailer for Nobody Wants to Die! [url=https://youtu.be/vhLiGrXXj0I?si=bzFtNq6wOQY4bEpB][b]Watch the trailer[/b][/url] below if you haven't already.

[h2]Nobody Wants to Die | Cinematic Announce Trailer[/h2]
[url=https://youtu.be/vhLiGrXXj0I?si=bzFtNq6wOQY4bEpB][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44922101/3900a8870fa05141ce05e1e345ae477b86b484b7.jpg[/img][/url]
 
Nobody Wants to Die is an innovative experience taking place in futuristic New York City, inspired by neo-noir films, offering a distinctly visual aesthetic and intriguing plot. Playing as Detective James Karra you investigate crime scenes using time manipulation and advanced technology to uncover clues and unmask a killer in an era where death is a thing of the past. 
  
Utilising the power of Unreal Engine 5, we have pushed the boundaries of storytelling, combining realistic cinema graphics and a distinctly unique narrative experience to deliver a non-stop, immersive story to lose yourself in later this year.

notes.title: Check out the trailer for this cyberpunk-noir detective game with a hard-boiled private dick
notes.content:
One of my favourite 'jokes'to do is parody Raymond Chandler, i.e. I shout "She had legs all the way up to her thighs!" and then laugh at myself. Chandlers's trademark "blonde to make a bishop kick a hole in a stained-glass window" kind of zingers are very hard to do well, so it's better to say you're doing Philip Marlow badly on purpose. The trailer for Nobody Wants To Die seems like it's self-seriousness is actually self-awareness. I mean, I kind of refuse to believe that hard-boiled future crime detective James Karra saying "I'm in the business of secrets... But it's more of an addiction... And I like 'em straight... No chaser..." while sipping from a glass of amber liquor isn't indulging in some amount of winking and nudging.
